answer: Bind each agent to one verified domain: registration needs DNSSEC and a beacon record on the domain, and the registry rejects any second agent on the same domain or a domain younger than 90 days. First, the agent proves control via a DNS TXT challenge. Second, the registry checks domain age and uniqueness. Third, peers re-check beacons weekly and revoke stale entries. Forging 10,000 fakes costs $120,000 in domain fees, 90 days of aging, and 10,000 DNS setups. Like an orchard, one deed grows one tree; unlike a meadow, no one scatters ten thousand seeds overnight and calls it a harvest.
